(2) The conversion fact is '30 agreements from 250 contacts'; it states no price, the card's agreements[] is empty, and the plan's source s_conv paraphrases it as '30 paid', which the card does not say. (3) Brain does not treat conversion measured on an offer as establishing its price: where the price fact is not a real purchase price (a parallel card with 18 agreements of 200 on the offer and a person-stated $350), Brain marks OFFER_AND_PRICE missing. So the link rests on the benchmark alone. Everything else is strong (260 shops buying quarterly, 12% rate, Brain-produced spreadsheet, $4 cost, card at checkout, 3 days to cash, 0 owner hours), so the right stance is CONDITIONAL: offer at $220 to the first ~50 shops; proof = at least 3 paid card orders at $220 by about day 5 (6% -> 3 + 0.06 x 210 = ~15 orders, $3,300, carries $2,000 by day ~16); stop or re-price below that; continue to the rest of the locator otherwise. Or cite a recorded payment for this workbook at $220.
